- When sentiment is predominantly negative (0.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high or use 30-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (1.00) but price declines in next 3–5 days, model overreacts; apply mean reversion by subtracting 1–3% from forecast if sentiment shifts to neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.00/1.00), model exhibits erratic behavior; use 14-day rolling average to smooth forecast and avoid overfitting to short-term sentiment.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 70–72 range after 75+ peak), model exhibits “mean reversion bias”; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–7 days if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- Forecast horizon > 14 days: model tends to overestimate; apply 10–15% discount to long-term forecast if sentiment is weak or negative.
